description: Reading plans (the /plans/ pages, web/plans.js): each plan's id, its name in each interface language, and its days in order, each day the chapters to read as BOOK.chapter (Hebrew numbering for the Old Testament). The site offers a plan in a language only once every chapter in it is translated in that language, so a plan can be listed here before it is readable. The plans from bible-in-a-year on are made by scripts/build_plans.py, which cuts each outline into days of whole chapters balanced by verse count; change their outlines there and run it, not here. A plan may have a description, in English, saying how it is ordered; the site does not show it.

plans.description: The whole Bible in the order its events happened or, for poetry, prophecy and letters, the time they are usually dated to, on the outline most published chronological plans share. Job is read with the patriarchs, between Genesis 11 and 12, and Psalm 90 (“of Moses”) after Deuteronomy. 1–2 Samuel, 1–2 Kings and 1–2 Chronicles are interleaved event by event, Chronicles’ genealogies (1 Chronicles 1–10) at Saul’s death. Psalms whose titles name an event in David’s life are read beside it (59, 34, 56, 52, 57, 142, 54, 60, 51, 32, 3, 63, 18), as are those 1 Chronicles 16 quotes (96, 105, 106); the other psalms follow David’s last years (1 Chronicles 21–28), except Psalms 72 and 127 (“of Solomon”), read in his reign, Psalms 74, 79 and 137, read at the fall of Jerusalem, and Psalm 126, read at the return. Proverbs and the Song of Songs come in Solomon’s reign and Ecclesiastes in his old age (1 Kings 11). Each prophet is read in the reign his book names or the one most often proposed: Obadiah under Jehoram, Joel under Joash, Jonah under Jeroboam II (2 Kings 14:25), Amos and Hosea under Uzziah, Micah and Isaiah 1–35 under Ahaz, Isaiah 36–66 after Hezekiah, Nahum under Manasseh, Zephaniah and Habakkuk under Josiah, Jeremiah from Josiah to the fall of Jerusalem and Lamentations after it, then Ezekiel and Daniel in the exile. Ezra 1–6 comes with Haggai and Zechariah (Ezra 5:1), Esther between Ezra 6 and 7, then Ezra 7–10, Nehemiah and Malachi. The four Gospels are read whole, one after another, since a day is whole chapters and a harmony would cut them. Acts is interleaved with Paul’s letters where they were written: James before the Jerusalem council, Galatians after Acts 14, 1–2 Thessalonians after Acts 17, 1 Corinthians after Acts 19, 2 Corinthians and Romans after Acts 20, Ephesians, Colossians, Philemon and Philippians after Acts 28; then 1 Timothy, Titus, 1 Peter, Hebrews, 2 Timothy, 2 Peter, Jude, John’s letters and Revelation. Many of these dates are debated; this is one defensible order, not the only one. Days are whole chapters, balanced by verse count.
